purpose: The SECOND link of the land chain.  screen_land_parity.py proves the BOARD's footprint equals its LIBRARY MASTER, to the nanometre.  That is worth nothing on its own -- it only says the board agrees with a file.  This index says which drawing that file was ruled against, and where the ruling is written down.  Together the two links are: board land == library master == manufacturer/IPC drawing.

tiers.1: manufacturer drawing read, document number and dimensions recorded; a tier-1 row MUST carry `drawing` and `confirmed`
tiers.2A: vendor-specific stock footprint, drawing read at B-03 closure (FBV2-S2-002)
tiers.2_OPEN: vendor-specific stock footprint, drawing NOT re-read -- an OPEN item, not a pass
tiers.3: generic JEDEC / IPC package, correct by package identity

confirmed_in_this_index_pending.what: TIER-1 rows whose FIGURES are recorded in the normative ledger's prose (sections 1 / 2A / 2C) rather than in this index's machine-readable `confirmed` block.  LAND7 holds this list as an EQUALITY, so it may SHRINK and a NEW tier-1 row may not join it: a row added from here on must carry its own figures.

AQROOT_Beta:Ebyte_E07-400M10S.drawing: Ebyte E07-400M10S User Manual (cdebyte.com pdf-down id 1824), 11 pp, section 3 'Size and Pin definition' mechanical sheet + section 2.2 parameter table ("Interface method 1.27mm / Half hole", "Size 14*20mm")
AQROOT_Beta:Ebyte_E07-400M10S.ruled: D-762, replacing the citation that named no document

confirmed.what: U7 (E07-400M10S, 433 MHz CC1101) and U8 (E22-900M22S, 915 MHz SX1262) share ONE land identity's geometry, and until D-762 the weaker of the two citations read only "Ebyte manufacturer drawing, archived" -- no document, no revision, no figure.  Each module's OWN drawing was read INDEPENDENTLY and they agree figure for figure, which is WHY one land serves both.

drawing_states.module_solder_side_pad_mm: 0.90 inboard x 0.80 in the pitch direction, plus the 0.50 half-hole outboard (E07 sheet: "Bottom pad: 0.90 / 0.50 / 0.80")

board_and_master.terminals: 22 lands, columns at x = +/- 7.000 -- i.e. ON the 14.0 mm body edge, so each land straddles its half-hole
board_and_master.land_mm: 1.80 across the body edge x 0.90 in the pitch direction
board_and_master.first_and_last_terminal_y_mm: +8.000 and -9.000 about the body centre, i.e. 2.000 from the top edge and 1.000 from the bottom edge of a 20.000 mm body
board_and_master.verdict: EVERY POSITIONAL FIGURE EXACT ON BOTH MODULES.  The land is 0.90 inboard -- the module pad exactly -- plus a DELIBERATE 0.40 mm outboard toe beyond the 0.50 half-hole for the solder fillet, and 0.05 mm per side in the pitch direction (0.90 against the module's 0.80), leaving a 0.37 mm land-to-land gap.

confirmed.pin_map_cross_check: Verified pin by pin on the board against each vendor pin table, 44 pins, all correct.  E07: 1-5/11/12/20/22 GND, 6-8/10/13 NC, 9 VCC = +3V3, 14 GDO2 unused, 15 GDO0, 16 MISO, 17 MOSI, 18 SCK, 19 CSN, 21 ANT unused (the IPEX port carries the antenna).  E22: 6 RXEN, 7 TXEN and 8 DIO2 SHORTED together, 9 VCC, 12 GND, 13 DIO1, 14 BUSY, 15 NRST, 16-19 SPI, 21 ANT unused.  The E22 short is the vendor's own option and its note 1 makes it a FIRMWARE requirement -- carried as policy key SX1262_TXEN_IS_DIO2 in Firmware/src/hw/aqroot_demo_board.json.
confirmed.a_source_that_disagrees_with_itself: cdebyte.com's E22-900M22S web pin table lists NRST on pin 12 AND on pin 15.  This board GROUNDS pin 12, so read that way the 915 MHz radio would be held in permanent reset.  The current E22-M Series User Manual section 3.2 -- archived here -- says pin 12 is GND and NRST is pin 15 only.  THE MANUAL IS THE AUTHORITY AND THE BOARD IS RIGHT; the web table is wrong, and it is written down here so the next reader does not chase it.

confirmed.why_this_one: SOT-563 is the most load-bearing tier-3 row on the board: it carries U21, the SWITCHED 5 V ACCESSORY BOOST that Demo scope REQUIRES, and D2/D4/D5, the TPD4E1B06 ESD arrays that stand on the USB and community-port contacts.  A 0.5 mm-pitch power package is not a chip resistor, and 'correct by package identity' is a category claim, not a measurement.

deltas_measured_not_assumed.row_separation: 1.425 vs 1.48 -> -0.055, i.e. each land sits 0.0275 mm further inboard
deltas_measured_not_assumed.net_effect_on_the_joint: heel 0.225 mm under the 1.2 mm body against TI's 0.195, and toe 0.250 mm past the 0.8 mm terminal tip against TI's 0.275 -- MORE HEEL, SLIGHTLY LESS TOE, same pitch.

confirmed.verdict: ACCEPTED AS A LEGITIMATE ALTERNATIVE, NOT AS A MATCH.  TI's own note 5 on that sheet says 'Publication IPC-7351 may have alternate designs', and the KiCad land IS the IPC-7351 design for SOT-563.  Every divergence is <= 0.055 mm, none of them reduces terminal coverage, the 0.150 mm land-to-land gap is ordinary for 0.5 mm pitch and is above this board's class floor, and real KiCad DRC reports zero clearance violations.  The figures are recorded here so the next reader compares numbers instead of re-deriving them.

U1.was: lib_footprint_mismatch -- the footprint-embedded ANTENNA KEEP-OUT rule area's copper-layer set: the master writes `*.Cu`, the board's copy named F.Cu / B.Cu / In1.Cu / In2.Cu because KiCad clamped the shorthand to the stackup the board had when U1 was placed and never re-expanded it when In3.Cu and In4.Cu were added.  62 of 62 pads were always identical.
U1.closed: D-617.  The board's copy now writes `*.Cu`, the string the master itself writes, so it cannot be clamped again by a future stackup change.  KiCad reports ZERO lib_footprint_mismatch and `lib_footprint_mismatch` has been removed from verify_promotion.INHERITED -- if it returns it must fail loudly.
U1.cost: Two nets were re-laid by the router under the widened rule: /01_POWER_TREE/USB_VBUS_CHG (two chains, 52.013 -> 49.505 mm and 12.657 -> 13.259 mm, still In3.Cu, no barrel) and Net-(SW9-A) (110.000 -> 69.955 mm, 4 vias, In3.Cu footprint 110.000 -> 50.999 mm).  Ledger 57 -> 57 open edges, ratsnest 73 -> 73, parity 247 -> 247.
